ledgerSearch.outcome: CTD-0055 is decisive across Part IV: the corpus describes Providence as already self-sovereign, device-local, unowned, and capture-resistant, and the item requires every such property to be stated as a requirement rather than a current fact until the protocol, threat model, and controls are published. CTD-0006 requires that no physiological measure determine governance standing, which governs the trust layer and the AI prohibitions. CTD-0012 keeps Bio-Consensus, COHERENCE, and the Currency of Presence distinct. CTD-0027 records that the AI integration decision process is undefined. CTD-0072 requires that nothing sound operational. CTD-0007 governs the self-epigraphs.

findings.summary: Each of the four functions lost the property that makes it constitutional.

evidence.baseline: No part of this function is owned by the application operator. The identity belongs to the participant. ... The attestation system is implemented on the common trust infrastructure rather than as a proprietary reputation system owned by the application operator. ... Contributions are attributed; access is open to all network participants; no single actor owns the commons or controls access to it.
evidence.shipped: (the four functions survive with their unresolved questions; the ownership properties do not)

findings.diagnosis: The item requires unimplemented properties to read as requirements. The baseline states them as flat assertions, which the item does reach, and the correct repair is the modal shift the restoration makes. What the paydown did instead was delete the properties and keep the unresolved questions, which leaves four functions with no constitutional content at all. A first version whose commons can be owned by its operator is not the thing the chapter specifies.

findings.summary: The coordination tools' design principle was removed.

evidence.baseline: The tools are designed for the governance processes the constitutional principles require, deliberation, consent, conflict repair, and stewardship accountability, rather than for the governance processes that are easiest to build.
evidence.shipped: Tools should support deliberation, consent, conflict repair, and stewardship without imposing one governance model.

findings.diagnosis: Rather than for the governance processes that are easiest to build is the design refusal, and it is the sentence a builder under deadline needs. The shipped version keeps the four processes and adds the no-single-model requirement, which is a real improvement and is kept.

reasoning.note: R-LEDGER-WINS. The ownership properties return in requirement grammar rather than as assertions of fact, which is what CTD-0055 asks for, and every shipped unresolved-question clause is kept beside them.
R-PUNCT-STRUCT. Two em dashes. Both were parenthetical appositives listing governance processes or knowledge base contents and both became comma pairs.

The shipped heading What the First Version Would Do, whose conditional carries the ledger's modality, and the shipped unresolved-question clauses on key recovery, revocation, third-party copies, exported records, universal scores, attribution, licensing, moderation, and stewardship.
The four ownership and commons properties, and the coordination tools' design refusal.

openQuestions: The volume-04 voice card was prepared by the same pass that produced the shipped text, and its exemplar anchors and protected lines quote that text rather than the baseline. The card records `Author approved: pending tone, strategy, heading, and overcompression review`. The restoration keeps every line the card protects and otherwise follows the baseline, which means card and source now diverge in wording the card does not name. R-VOICE-BIND requires that the disagreement be raised rather than settled here: the card should be re-derived from whichever text the author approves.

Structural labels were frozen for this pass and none was touched. Every markdown heading, every standalone bold display line, every chapter label, and every all-capital display line is byte identical to its pre-edit state, in the same order, with the same blank-line separators on both sides. A label determines a section id, a section id is a public route, and `publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json` already records this volume's renames and resolves the historical routes. Changing one is a continuity decision and not an editorial one. Only the running prose between labels was restored. Where a baseline label names its section better than the current one, the cost is recorded here and the label is left alone.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the shipped text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, the corpus voice card, the volume-04 voice card, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required. The clearest demonstration in the volume that deleting a claim is not the same as paying down a claim: CTD-0055 asks for a modality change and the pass performed a deletion, which satisfies the gate and loses the specification.

audits.auditor: editorial-agent, generation 2 of the twenty-rule re-render lane
audits.scope: Full re-read of the current section against the immutable baseline under all twenty rules. The original record was derived under the thirteen-rule index; this audit adds the substitution count and the later rules: R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY, R-CORRECTION-SCOPE, R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD, R-PAIRED-DELETION, R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT, and R-REFRAIN-COST.

substitutionTest.rule: R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, substitution form, run as standing procedure before any pairing test
substitutionTest.method: Normalize both texts, strip markup, split into sentences of three or more words, count baseline sentences appearing verbatim in the current section.
substitutionTest.note: Well above zero, so the section is a restoration, not a substitution, and the pairing test applies. Verbatim survival understates fidelity here: every R-PUNCT-STRUCT repair and recorded bounding changes the sentence it lands in, so the non-surviving remainder was read against the diff and attributed rather than assumed lost.

audits.checked: R-CAUTIOUS-HALF: each of the four functions keeps both its capability and its constitutional property, and the restored ownership properties keep their committing form inside the requirement grammar. R-PAIRED-DELETION: identity, attestation, commons contribution, and coordination were swept; each function pairs with the specification chapter and the prohibitions, ends aligned. R-CORRECTION-SCOPE: the CTD-0055 grammar re-verified at width; performs stands as would perform, the copula conversion the item requires, and the restored properties are otherwise baseline text. R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY re-run: the kept unresolved-question clauses on key recovery, revocation, third-party copies, exported records, universal scores, attribution, licensing, privacy, moderation, and stewardship were searched for in the immutable baseline and are not there; seeded canon with provenance visible in the original kept notes, CTD-0055 and CTD-0006 bounding, no credit. R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT: nothing else kept, no credit owed, stated explicitly. R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD, R-REFRAIN-COST, R-TENSE, R-DEIXIS, R-NEGATION-STACK: nothing fires.
audits.conclusion: The restoration holds under the full twenty-rule index. Nine of twelve baseline sentences survive verbatim; the remainder are the four em dash glyphs repaired at two sites, the would perform conversion, and the seeded unresolved-question clauses, all attributed. No prose change required.
